paragraphs: Heil designs and manufactures the bodies that go on garbage trucks, selling to the fleets that collect refuse. The range runs from front loaders and automated front loaders to rear loaders, automated side loaders, and multi-compartment rear loaders.

The bodies are made in the United States, at a plant in Fort Payne, Alabama, that the company calls home. The product the site leads with is the RevAMP, a fully electric automated side loader. It is described as running with an auger compactor and no hydraulics on route. A training programme called Nexteligence is built for service technicians working on the Heil product line.

The company dates itself to 1901 and says it has built its reputation in the solid waste industry since then. It began as the Heil Railjoint Welding Company, founded by Julius P. Heil. Heil was later acquired and became a subsidiary within Dover Corporation. Dover then combined Heil Environmental, Marathon Equipment Company, and Bayne Machine Works into Environmental Solutions Group. Terex Corporation acquired Environmental Solutions Group on October 8, 2024.
